overview.main_commercial_differentiation: Public Speaking Is a Skill You Practise — Not a Lecture You Attend.
overview.professional_learning_workflow: Understand Audience → Define Message → Prepare → Rehearse → Deliver → Engage → Receive Feedback → Improve
core_educational_principles: Clear communication matters more than theatrical performance.
Preparation matters more than memorized perfection.
Effective speech depends on audience and purpose.
Different speakers can have different effective styles.
Speaking anxiety is normal and manageable with practical preparation routines.

commercial_differentiation.heading: Practise Speaking. Get Useful Feedback. Apply It Again.

instructional_model.description: Short live demonstrations illustrating speech opening, structure, vocal pacing, audience interaction, common pitfalls, and practical improvements.
Interactive lab exercises where students deliver short responses, prepared introductions, storytelling drafts, vocal drills, and impromptu speeches.
Supportive breakout practice cohorts where participants listen, ask questions, give constructive feedback, and observe diverse speaking styles.
Specific, objective evaluations identifying what was effective, what was unclear, and 1–2 actionable priority improvements for the next rehearsal.
Opportunities to revise speech notes, adjust delivery based on critique, rehearse, and deliver the speech again to measure improvement.
Documenting preparation effectiveness, recording observations, audience reactions, and personal development goals.

key_differentiators.title: Repeated Speaking Practice
key_differentiators.description: Learn by actively delivering speeches rather than passively consuming speaking theory.

key_differentiators.title: Structured Speech Preparation
key_differentiators.description: Develop clear openings, organized central messages, credible supporting points, and memorable conclusions.

key_differentiators.title: Audience Interaction
key_differentiators.description: Practise spontaneous speaking, active listening, and composed responses to live audience questions.

key_differentiators.title: Individual Performance Feedback
key_differentiators.description: Review baseline and final speaking evidence with constructive, non-judgmental instructor critiques.

speaking_anxiety_education.heading: Learn Practical Ways to Prepare for Speaking Challenges.
speaking_anxiety_education.approved_copy: Explore realistic preparation strategies for managing common speaking nerves, including rehearsal, gradual practice, comfortable breathing, supportive feedback and familiarization with different audience settings.
appropriate_strategies: Rehearsing the opening lines aloud until comfortable
Using structured cue cards instead of memorizing scripts
Gradual exposure: speaking first to a single peer, then small groups
Testing audio and camera equipment before virtual sessions
Focusing on audience benefit and message clarity rather than self-evaluation
Embracing purposeful pauses to breathe and regain composure
Tracking observable skill improvements rather than aiming for perfection
unacceptable_claims: No claims of curing anxiety or eliminating stage fright entirely
No guarantees of instant charisma or commanding every room
No clinical diagnoses or psychological treatment claims
learner_safety: Zero forced disclosures of personal trauma or sensitive private matters
Safe, supportive environment free from harsh public criticism
Voluntary practice steps with instructor accommodations where needed

audience_engagement_framework.heading: Learn to Speak With an Audience, Not Just At One.

core_skills.name: Audience Awareness
core_skills.description: Analyzing listener expectations, interests, prior knowledge, and non-verbal reactions.

core_skills.name: Opening Engagement
core_skills.description: Establishing immediate relevance through compelling questions, relatable scenarios, or clear central themes.

core_skills.name: During the Speech
core_skills.description: Using conversational pacing, purposeful pauses, vocal emphasis, and logical transitions to maintain audience attention.

core_skills.name: Interactive Speaking
core_skills.description: Facilitating voluntary participant questions, quick informal polls, and inclusive discussions.

core_skills.name: Composed Q&A
core_skills.description: Listening attentively, clarifying ambiguous questions, answering directly with evidence, and acknowledging uncertainty honestly.

core_skills.name: Difficult Interaction
core_skills.description: Maintaining calm composure, de-escalating respectful disagreements, and redirecting discussions back to the speech topic.

multilingual_policy.approved_copy: Public speaking fundamentals may be taught and practised in English, Hindi or Gujarati where a suitable cohort and instructor are available. The language used for instruction and assessment will follow the selected batch's published delivery format.
rules: Instructor language capability and cohort language are verified before batch launch
Instruction and speech assessment are conducted in the advertised cohort language
Core public speaking competencies and portfolio standards remain rigorous across all language options
No assumption of advanced English fluency for regional-language cohorts

virtual_and_recorded_speaking.heading: Build Speaking Skills for Live, Online and Recorded Audiences.
live_speaking: Audience orientation and natural eye engagement
Time management and live audience interaction
virtual_speaking: Camera setup, eye-level framing, and appropriate lighting
Microphone check and clear audio quality
Screen sharing and presenting with virtual platforms (Zoom / Google Meet)
Managing chat questions and remote audience engagement
recorded_speaking: Framing and audio testing for asynchronous speech reviews
Using speech timers during recorded rehearsals
Structured self-review of recorded practice videos
Secure, consent-governed storage of practice files

responsible_ai_policy.heading: Use AI for Rehearsal. Keep Your Speaking Authentic.
responsible_ai_policy.approved_copy: Use accessible AI tools for speech outlining, practice questions, rehearsal and feedback where available. Verify facts and preserve your own voice, ideas and authentic delivery.
appropriate_uses: Brainstorming speech topics and audience angles
Drafting speech outlines and logical flow structures
Generating potential audience questions for Q&A practice
Simulating impromptu speaking prompts for rehearsal
Reviewing speech transcripts for clarity and concise wording
mandatory_human_verification: Verify all facts, statistics, citations, and quotes manually
Preserve personal authenticity, genuine stories, and individual speaking voice
Never generate entire speeches with AI to read verbatim
Protect privacy: do not input proprietary or sensitive personal information into AI tools

safe_ai_prompts.prompt: Help me organize a 5-minute informative speech on [topic] for [audience]. Suggest a hook, 3 main points with transitions, and a conclusion.
Give me 3 realistic impromptu speaking topics suitable for a 2-minute response using the PREP (Point, Reason, Example, Point) framework.
I am delivering a speech on [topic]. List 5 thoughtful questions and 2 challenging or skeptical questions an audience might ask.
Review this draft speech transcript for clarity, sentence length, and natural spoken transitions. Do not rewrite my personal style.

privacy_and_recording_safeguards.consent_policy: All video/audio recordings require explicit participant consent. Recordings are used exclusively for individual learning feedback and academic assessment.
privacy_and_recording_safeguards.storage_policy: Recordings are stored securely with restricted access and are never shared publicly or used in promotional materials without express written authorization.
privacy_and_recording_safeguards.student_privacy: Learners are never required to disclose sensitive personal matters, financial details, or confidential workplace information in speech assignments.

inclusive_assessment.principles: Evaluation focuses on observable communication competencies, clear messaging, and listener comprehension rather than physical appearance, personality extroversion, or accent conformity.
inclusive_assessment.accommodations: Supports diverse learning needs including seated presentations, adjustable camera setups, varied audience sizes, and assistive speaking technologies.

best_for: Beginners and intermediate speakers seeking structured speaking practice
Educators, trainers, and facilitators addressing groups and classes
Professionals and team coordinators presenting in meetings and events
Entrepreneurs and startup founders pitching ideas and projects
Content creators seeking presence and clarity on video and podcasts
Students preparing for academic presentations and public forums
not_for: Individuals seeking medical or clinical treatment for severe social anxiety disorders
Those looking for accent-elimination or native-speaker voice imitation courses
Students seeking advanced presentation software and graphic slide design training (take Course 89)
Anyone expecting instant keynote celebrity status without repeated speaking practice

prerequisites: Ability to communicate basic ideas in the selected cohort language (English, Hindi, or Gujarati)
Willingness to participate in supportive, small-group speaking exercises and receive constructive feedback
Basic computer or smartphone with functioning camera and microphone for live labs and recording practice
No prior public speaking experience or advanced English fluency required
highlights: 5 Weeks of intensive speech preparation, vocal delivery, storytelling, and audience engagement (40 guided hours)
Build the complete Public Speaking & Audience Engagement Portfolio: 4 assessed speeches, baseline & final evaluations, instructor critiques, and improvement plan
Master speech planning and structure: compelling openings, central message formulation, supporting evidence, clear transitions, and memorable conclusions
Learn structured storytelling for speaking: personal anecdotes, illustrative examples, authentic delivery, and audience takeaways
Develop voice, presence and delivery: speaking pace, intentional pauses, vocal emphasis, comfortable gestures, audience eye contact, and camera presence
Excel in impromptu speaking: PREP framework (Point, Reason, Example, Point), short thinking pauses, adaptability under pressure, and graceful mistake recovery
Engage live and virtual audiences: active listening, voluntary participation, clear Q&A responses, and respectful handling of difficult interactions
Multilingual cohort delivery: practical instruction and assessment supported in English, Hindi, or Gujarati based on verified batch availability
hands_on_tech: Zoom or Google Meet for live speaking labs and breakout practice
Smartphone or webcam recording device for self-review
Speech timer / stopwatch for time management
Speaking cue cards for structured notes
Optional AI assistant for outline drafting and practice question generation
learning_outcomes: Preparing an informative or persuasive speech.

portfolio.title: Public Speaking & Audience Engagement Portfolio
portfolio.description: A comprehensive, practical public speaking portfolio demonstrating baseline assessment, narrative storytelling, spontaneous impromptu delivery, persuasive/informative speech presentation, audience Q&A interaction, documented feedback, and an ongoing personal development plan.

deliverables.name: Performance 01: Two-Minute Introduction Speech
deliverables.description: Introduce oneself or a chosen relevant topic clearly to a small audience. Focuses on baseline clarity, speech organization, audibility, natural pacing, and goal setting.

deliverables.name: Performance 02: Three-Minute Storytelling Speech
deliverables.description: Communicate a meaningful experience, illustrative case, or relevant story with a structured narrative sequence, audience relevance, and clear moral or practical takeaway.

deliverables.name: Performance 03: Two-Minute Impromptu Talk
deliverables.description: Respond to an unfamiliar instructor-supplied prompt with limited preparation using structured spontaneous speaking frameworks (such as PREP) and graceful pause recovery.
evidence: Learner self-reflection on composure and adaptability

deliverables.name: Performance 04: Five-to-Seven-Minute Final Speech & Q&A
deliverables.description: Deliver a fully prepared, rehearsed Informative or Persuasive speech to an audience, followed by a live question-and-answer session demonstrating active listening and composure.
required_elements: Defined audience profile and clear speech objective
Three well-developed supporting points with verified evidence
Professional vocal delivery and physical presence
Live audience Q&A handling with composed, evidence-based responses
evidence: Speech planning brief and verified outline
Rehearsal notes and peer review feedback
Final recorded speech and Q&A exchange

improvement_framework.title: Baseline vs. Final Speaking Assessment
improvement_framework.description: An evidence-based improvement framework comparing common communication competencies between initial baseline performance and final capstone delivery.

assessment_model.title: Speaking Assessment Rubric

breakdown.area: Final speech, feedback integration and improvement plan

criteria: Clarity and focus of central message
Appropriate supporting examples and verified evidence
Vocal delivery: audibility, pacing, and intentional pauses
Audience orientation, eye contact, and comfortable gestures
Time management and adherence to speech limits
Audience questions, active listening, and respectful interaction
Receptivity to feedback and observable progress over time
unacceptable_criteria: Natural accent suppression or native-speaker imitation
Total absence of nervousness or minor speech disfluencies
Automated AI score replacements for human evaluation
Audience applause volume or social media metrics

modules.title: Speech Foundations & Speaking Anxiety
modules.objective: Understand public speaking fundamentals, assess baseline communication and learn practical preparation strategies for managing common speaking concerns.

lessons.title: Normalizing Speaking Challenges
topics: Nervousness does not always prevent good communication.

modules.handsOnLab:
Conduct short, supportive speaking exercises and a baseline introduction assessment.

Students practise:

- Introducing themselves.
- Speaking at an understandable pace.
- Using a simple outline.
- Maintaining a clear message.
- Finishing a short speaking task.
modules.assignment:
Complete the first major assessed portfolio performance:

**Performance 01 — Two-Minute Introduction Speech**

Also prepare:

1. Baseline observation record.
2. Initial speaking goal.
3. Preparation checklist.
4. Personal reflection.
modules.businessApplication: Student introductions, basic professional introductions, classroom speaking and small-group presentations.
modules.importantRule:
This module teaches everyday speech preparation and practical coping strategies.

It is NOT a psychological treatment program.

Students who experience significant distress may need appropriate professional support beyond this course.

---

modules.title: Speech Structure & Storytelling

lessons.title: Authenticity

lessons.title: Audience Comprehension
topics: Does every detail support the topic?

modules.handsOnLab:
Students create and share short personal stories.

Practise:

- A logical sequence.

**Performance 02 — Three-Minute Storytelling Speech**

2. Audience.
3. Story outline.

lessons.title: Virtual Camera Presence

modules.handsOnLab:

2. Pausing practice.

lessons.title: Audience Participation

faq.question: What is Public Speaking & Audience Engagement?
faq.answer: It is a practical course that teaches speech preparation, storytelling, vocal delivery, impromptu speaking and audience interaction through guided speaking practice.

faq.question: Is the course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed for learners with the ability to communicate basic ideas in the selected teaching language.

faq.question: Do I need fluent English?
faq.answer: No. General public-speaking skills can be taught and assessed in an available English, Hindi or Gujarati cohort.

faq.question: Are Hindi and Gujarati batches available?
faq.answer: Language options depend on verified instructor and cohort availability. Students should check the current batch's advertised language.

faq.question: How long is the course?
faq.answer: Five weeks with 40 guided learning hours.

faq.question: What is the fee?
faq.answer: ₹5,900, subject to Nova Skills' verified pricing and tax policy.

faq.question: Will I practise speaking in class?
faq.answer: Yes. Instructor-led speaking labs and small-group audience practice are central parts of the curriculum.

faq.question: Will the course eliminate stage fright?
faq.answer: No. It teaches practical preparation and speaking strategies, but individual anxiety levels and progress vary.

faq.question: Will I learn speech structure?
faq.answer: Yes. You will practise openings, main messages, supporting points, transitions and conclusions.

faq.question: Will I learn storytelling?
faq.answer: Yes. You will prepare and deliver a three-minute storytelling speech.

faq.question: Will I learn impromptu speaking?
faq.answer: Yes. You will practise short talks with limited preparation and complete a two-minute impromptu assessment.

faq.question: Will I learn voice control?
faq.answer: You will practise speaking pace, pauses, emphasis, comfortable breathing and understandable vocal delivery.

faq.question: Will I learn body language?
faq.answer: Yes. The course covers comfortable posture, gestures, audience orientation and virtual camera presence.

faq.question: Must I maintain eye contact with everyone?
faq.answer: No. Audience engagement can take different forms. The course assesses effective communication rather than rigid eye-contact rules.

faq.question: Will I practise audience questions?
faq.answer: Yes. The course includes active listening, clarification, respectful disagreement and answering unexpected questions.

faq.question: How many major speeches will I deliver?
faq.answer: Four: a two-minute introduction, three-minute story, two-minute impromptu talk and five-to-seven-minute final speech.

faq.question: Will I receive feedback?
faq.answer: Yes. The curriculum includes instructor critique, peer evaluation, recorded review and improvement planning.

faq.question: Will my speaking be recorded?
faq.answer: Recorded practice supports assessment, subject to appropriate consent, privacy requirements and approved alternatives.

faq.question: Do I need a paid recording application?
faq.answer: No. An appropriate phone or computer recording method may be used.

faq.question: Will I learn virtual speaking?
faq.answer: Yes. The course introduces camera framing, microphone use, online audience interaction and basic technical preparation.

faq.question: Can AI help me practise speeches?
faq.answer: Yes. AI may help with outlines, rehearsal questions and draft review, but final evaluation is instructor-led.

faq.question: Will AI evaluate my confidence?
faq.answer: AI tools may provide limited feedback, but they are not reliable measures of personality, mental health or overall speaking ability.

faq.question: Does this course teach PowerPoint slide design?
faq.answer: No. Advanced slide design and presentation production are part of separate specializations.

faq.question: Is this different from Presentation Skills & Business Storytelling?
faq.answer: Yes. Course 89 emphasizes slide-supported communication; Course 90 emphasizes speech delivery and interaction with audiences.

faq.question: Will I become a professional speaker after five weeks?
faq.answer: The course builds practical speaking foundations. Professional speaking careers require further experience and opportunities.

faq.question: What will my final portfolio include?
faq.answer: Four assessed speaking performances, baseline/final evaluation, documented feedback, revisions and a personalized development plan.

faq.question: Is this useful for teachers and trainers?
faq.answer: Yes. The skills can support classroom explanations, training sessions and audience-facing communication.

faq.question: Is this useful for entrepreneurs and creators?
faq.answer: Yes. Speech preparation, storytelling and audience interaction are relevant to pitches, events, videos and community communication.  ---
